summary.headline: Triveni H1 FY27 PBT swung to ₹131 crore from a ₹25 crore loss, driven by sugar realisations up 9% to ₹4,428/MT.
summary.overview: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue rose 5% YoY to ₹3,311 crore and operating margin expanded 383 bps to 6.9%, with PBT of ₹131 crore versus a loss of ₹25 crore. Q2 revenue rose 8% to ₹1,731 crore. Sugar drove the turnaround on higher realisations, lower inventory and lower finance cost, while net debt fell to ₹157 crore from ₹702 crore a year ago. Management flagged a mixed H2: tight domestic sugar stocks support prices, but the ESY 26-27 ethanol tender resets alcohol economics and the Water business needs faster execution.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 5% to ₹2,497 crore; realisation up 9% to ₹4,428/MT, dispatches stable at 5.33 lakh MT. Q2 realisation up 16% to ₹4,728/MT with dispatches down 8%. Closing inventory 1.03 lakh MT vs 1.69 lakh MT a year ago, valued at ₹38.6/kg.

segments.name: Alcohol (Distillery)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue up 3%, PBIT up 44%; Q2 net revenue up 19% on 16% higher volume. H1 production 1,085 lakh litres, down 13% YoY, due to fewer operating days, storage constraints and a shift away from B-heavy molasses. Grain-based ethanol is the largest component.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: H1 revenue down 17% and Q2 down 13%; H1 PBIT ₹3 crore vs ₹13 crore, Q2 roughly breakeven. Closing order book ₹1,452 crore: ₹404 crore EPC/equipment and ₹1,048 crore long-duration O&M.

guidance_outlook: Sugar: management expects prevailing prices (about ₹5,800/quintal institutional, ₹5,400/quintal trade) to hold for the next couple of quarters, subject to no new government price or sale regulation; flagged a slight downward bias in the short term.

Alcohol: Q3 FY27 seen as relatively unabated versus internal estimates; Q4 FY27 profitability is hard to call until the ESY 26-27 tender is finalised. Maize at ₹26-27/kg may fully erode maize-ethanol profitability for standalone plants.
Water: expects execution to pick up in Q3 and Q4 FY27 and return to budgeted levels.
Capex: no meaningful capex planned for the year beyond minor steam and efficiency measures; board to wait at least one quarter of cash generation before evaluating other capital allocation options.

Management's own estimate of domestic 2026-27 net sugar production is about 27.5 million MT with downside risk, against opening stocks of about 3.5 million MT and consumption of about 28.5 million MT.
capex_capacity: Chandanpur plant started crushing on the call day (3 Nov 2026); Sabitgarh expected to start the next day, Khatauli on 6 Nov, and remaining plants shortly after Deepawali. Group has eight UP factories.
Early-season recoveries are running about 50-70 bps lower YoY on sampling data for UP as a whole; management says two of its eight factories are sharply affected while six are broadly fine.
Share of 238 cane variety is under 30% group-wide, with East UP near zero and Central UP single digit; management plans a sharp cut in the next planting.
Chandanpur and other factories' sugar recoveries will be confirmed by lab data after crushing begins; mid-December to mid-January is the window for a clear crop-impact assessment.
demand_pricing: Raw sugar import parity into Delhi, without margin, is about ₹54.5/kg; white sugar parity is about ₹59.15/kg (Dec contract) and ₹60.7/kg (Mar contract).
India has an import allowance of 1 million MT; about 300,000 MT has been imported so far. Management expects a further allowance of at least 2 million MT, mainly raw sugar.

October domestic prices averaged about ₹49/kg before rising sharply in November. Haryana SAP raised by ₹15 to ₹430/quintal for 26-27 and ₹20 to ₹450 for 27-28; UP cane price announcement expected in about three to four weeks.

ESY 26-27 OMC tender: 1,100 crore litres offered, with no offers for juice, syrup or B-heavy molasses ethanol. FCI rice capped at 30% (vs about 40% last year). Maize ethanol price cut by ₹3/litre in the tender.
Management's first-tranche split: ₹150 crore C-heavy, ₹324 crore FCI rice, up to ₹160 crore DFG, and about ₹466 crore maize (implied). Triveni's ethanol capacity is about 25 crore litres.

Global: raw sugar moved from $0.1331/lb (April low) to a $0.213 high and is about $0.195/lb; white sugar from $376/t to $561/t, now about $520/t. Brazil crop rebound and crude above $100/bbl are the key swing factors.

qa_highlights.question: How much damage has late UP rainfall done to the crop, and how does it compare with Maharashtra and Karnataka?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said damage is hard to quantify and could come as yield loss (lodging) or sucrose loss. Western UP cane is bound, so lodging risk is low. Sampling data shows about 50-70 bps lower recovery YoY for the state, with a clearer read by mid-December to mid-January.

qa_highlights.question: Will the tender-based ethanol economics hold once maize prices stay high?
qa_highlights.answer: Current maize at ₹26-27/kg would fully erode maize-ethanol profitability for standalone plants; integrated multi-feed players are better placed. Triveni procured maize at lower prices earlier, so Q3 is secure, and Q4 depends on the final tender.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for UP cane price and sugar import volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: UP cane price expected around end-November, with no number given. About 300,000 MT of the 1 million MT import allowance has been used, with at least 2 million MT more expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost rise despite the power transmission demerger?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Suresh Taneja said last year's comparatives show power transmission costs under discontinued operations, so the like-for-like comparison shows no significant increase. Management attributed the rise to the new labour code revising wages for 4,000-plus employees.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company deploy capital given high profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: No meaningful capex is planned. Debt reduction is a priority, but the board wants at least one quarter of cash generation data before deciding on other options.

risks_watch: Sugar crop uncertainty: UP late-season rain, Maharashtra and Karnataka water stress and drought, and seed-cane shortfall for 27-28.
ESY 26-27 ethanol tender may still be modified; maize prices at ₹26-27/kg and a ₹3/litre cut in maize price could compress Q4 FY27 alcohol profitability.
Government intervention on sugar prices (stock limits, quotas, import policy), which management said could change the price outlook.
Brazil crop rebound, crude above $100/bbl, and possible El Nino impact on Thailand and Australia could alter global prices.
Water segment execution: revenue down 17% in H1 with order book of ₹1,452 crore needing timely delivery in Q3-Q4.
summary.management_tone: Confident on sugar and the H1 turnaround, with figures stated firmly. Cautious and evasive on ethanol Q4 and the tender outcome, which management called too early to quantify. Candid that the Water business needs faster execution.
key_quotes: The first half reflects a meaningful improvement in operating performance and profitability.
The net debt level improved significantly to ₹157 crores as of the 30th of September 2026 compared to ₹702 crores a year ago
I think the sampling data is certainly indicating approximately at 50 basis to 70 basis point decline year-on-year in terms of sampling data.

growth.why: No numeric revenue guidance; management expects sugar prices to hold for a couple of quarters and Water to return to budget in Q3-Q4 FY27, but the ethanol tender reset and early-season recovery dip (50-70 bps lower) temper the outlook, with no meaningful capex planned.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Sugar prices (~₹5,800/quintal institutional) expected to hold for a couple of quarters, but H1 operating margin rose 383 bps to 6.9%, and the ESY 26-27 tender (maize at ₹26-27/kg, ₹3/litre cut) could compress Q4 FY27 alcohol profitability while management flags a slight downward price bias.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new capacity beyond restarting existing UP sugar plants after the 2026-27 season; management said no meaningful capex is planned for the year.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Early-season UP recoveries are 50-70 bps lower YoY, Q2 sugar dispatches fell 8%, and H1 alcohol production was down 13%; Water execution must recover to budget in Q3-Q4 FY27 from H1 revenue down 17%.

rows.label: New capex announcement

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: ESY 26-27 tender resets alcohol economics, maize at ₹26-27/kg may erode standalone ethanol profitability, and UP crop damage could cut recoveries 50-70 bps; Q4 profitability is unclear.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new products, brands or molecules were discussed.

rows.label: Net debt cut to ₹157 crore
rows.why: Net debt fell to ₹157 crore at 30 Sep 2026 from ₹702 crore a year ago, with cost of funds at 6.8% and finance cost down 20% YoY.

rows.label: Water order book recovery to budget
rows.why: Water order book is ₹1,452 crore (₹404 crore EPC, ₹1,048 crore O&M), and management expects execution to return to budgeted levels in Q3 and Q4 FY27 after H1 revenue fell 17%.

rows.label: Sugar import parity supports domestic prices
rows.why: Raw sugar import parity into Delhi is about ₹54.5/kg versus October domestic prices near ₹49/kg, and a further 2 million MT import allowance is expected, which could cap the upside.

tone.note: Management was confident on sugar realisations, the H1 turnaround and debt reduction, but cautious on Q4 ethanol profitability and the tender outcome, and candid that Water needs faster execution; analysts probed UP crop damage, maize-ethanol economics, and capital allocation.
